nodes.summary: Birkhoff–James orthogonality to `y` is equivalent to the existence of a functional in the duality mapping at `x` that vanishes at `y`.
nodes.title: Duality-mapping characterization of Birkhoff–James orthogonality

nodes.summary: For `x ≠ 0`, Birkhoff–James orthogonality to `y` is equivalent to the existence of a norming functional of `x` vanishing at `y`.
nodes.title: Norming-functional characterization of Birkhoff–James orthogonality

nodes.summary: In an inner product space, Birkhoff–James orthogonality is ordinary inner-product orthogonality.
nodes.title: Birkhoff–James orthogonality in inner product spaces

nodes.summary: If a norming functional of `x` vanishes at `y`, then `x` is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to `y`.
nodes.title: Annihilating norming functional implies Birkhoff–James orthogonality

nodes.summary: A vector is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to itself if and only if it is `0`.
nodes.title: Only zero is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to itself

nodes.summary: Birkhoff–James orthogonality is homogeneous in both arguments.
nodes.title: Homogeneity of Birkhoff–James orthogonality

nodes.summary: `0` is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to every vector.
nodes.title: Zero is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to every vector

nodes.summary: Every vector is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to `0`.
nodes.title: Every vector is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to zero

nodes.summary: `x` is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to `y` if `x` is a shortest vector on the affine line `x + 𝕜 • y`.
nodes.title: Birkhoff–James orthogonality

nodes.summary: The duality mapping is nonempty at every point: take a Hahn–Banach norming functional and scale it by `‖x‖`.
nodes.title: Duality mapping is nonempty

nodes.summary: The duality mapping (duality set) at `x`: the functionals `f` with `f x = ‖x‖ ^ 2` and `‖f‖ = ‖x‖`. At `x = 0` this is the singleton `{0}`.
nodes.title: Duality mapping of a normed space

nodes.summary: The converse: if `x ≠ 0` is Birkhoff–James orthogonal to `y`, there is a norming functional of `x` vanishing at `y`. Birkhoff–James orthogonality makes the distance from `x` to `𝕜 ∙ y` equal to `‖x‖`, so the dual distance formula supplies an annihilating norming functional.
nodes.title: Birkhoff–James orthogonality gives an annihilating norming functional

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
